_description: Reproduce the potentiation-actualization model from Blount et al. (2008/2012). The Cit+ phenotype evolved in 1 of 12 LTEE populations (Ara-3) at ~31,500 generations. Replay experiments showed that the probability of Cit+ evolving was near-zero from early clones but increased in later clones, demonstrating historical contingency. This implies a multi-step model: a potentiating mutation (rate λ₁) must occur before the actualizing mutation (rate λ₂) can produce the Cit+ phenotype.
_groundspring_question: Is the evolution of key innovations a simple single-step process, or does it require historical contingency (potentiating mutations)? The two-hit model explains both the rarity of Cit+ across populations and the increasing probability from later replay clones.
_cross_spring: lithoSpore module 4 (rare-event innovation), groundSpring B1 (neutral baseline), groundSpring B3 (clonal interference context)

_ltee_guidestone.blocks: Pillar 4 lithoSpore expansion — rare event statistics

model._description: Two-hit potentiation-actualization cascade: simulate N independent LTEE populations. Each generation, an un-potentiated population gains potentiation with probability p_pot per generation. Once potentiated, the Cit+ phenotype arises with probability p_act per generation. We simulate replay experiments by freezing populations at various timepoints and replaying from those states.

expected_results._cit_note: In the real LTEE, 1/12 populations evolved Cit+. With stochastic rates calibrated to synthetic params, we expect a low but nonzero fraction.
expected_results._potentiation_note: After 60,000 generations with p_pot=2e-6/gen, potentiation fraction = 1 - exp(-0.12) ≈ 11%. With 12 pops, typically 0-3 potentiated.
